newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia rural commodity prices slip-NFF/Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Australia rural commodity prices slip-NFF/Dresdner.

text.p: Australian rural commodity prices in Special Drawing Rights (SDR) terms fell by 0.5 percent in May despite rising wool prices, the National Farmers' Federation-Dresdner Australia Ltd Commodity Price Index shows.
But SDR prices are still 4.1 percent higher than a year ago, NFF director economic policy, Todd Ritchie, said.
Wool prices reached a two and a half year high in May with the Eastern Market Indicator climbing to 675 cents a kg clean clean, he said.
While wool prices rose by 5.3 percent in the month, this was offset by continued weakness in beef and grain prices, he said.
The overall index fell by 0.4 percent in May but was now 2.7 percent higher than a year ago, Ritchie said.
In Australian dollar terms the index was unchanged in May and 0.3 percent higher than 12 months ago, he said.
Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said non-rural SDR prices declined by 0.4 percent in May and were now 1.4 percent higher than a year ago.
In Australian dollar terms the index during the month was one percent lower than a year ago, he said.

"There has been a significant widening of the gap between the trade weighted index and the Australian dollar in the period from December 1 to May. This was a result of the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against most other currencies over that period," he said.

The solid uptrend of the world SDR price index for commodities since the beginning of the year partially reflected the U.S. dollar's strength, although since the beginning of May the trend appeared to have reversed somewhat, Henderson said.

The Australian dollar had traded lower against the U.S. dollar since the beginnuing of the year because of speculation in Australia of lower interest rates and in the U.S. of higher interest rates, he said.
In the second half of 1997 commodity prices could push higher and this could provide the platform for a solid rebound in the currency, he said.
